column2: A DETAIL HOP THAT RE-FETCHES ITS OWN URL. Found 2026-10-25 by asking the whole tree a question first measured on one row.
It started at us-sf-311-open311-requests, whose open item was "measure a hostgate gap for the detail hops" - the row's own
notice reported them refused. The prior question is what the hop brought back. Open311 GeoReport v2 defines ONE representation
of a service request, so /requests/<id>.json is its single-resource form and not a deeper record: measured against four SF
cases chosen to differ (open/closed, with and without media_url, with and without status_notes) and against the other Open311
server in the tree (spot.brooklinema.gov), the list and detail representations are the same keys with identical values every
time. 48 of that row's 59 requests a run were buying nothing, and 1,026 of 1,074 records carried _detail_pending - a
disclosure that there was more behind the record, when there was not.
Asking it statically of all 627 rows that declare a detail_url - no requests at all - found 16 whose detail_url IS their url.
7 were removed with the Open311 work; the 9 below were each then MEASURED, one request, because "your detail_url is your own
endpoint" is NECESSARY for a worthless hop and not SUFFICIENT: a key naming a different id reaches a different document
through the same endpoint, which is a real thing to want.
make lint-sources fails the shape now (detail-self-hop). Its first predicate was OVER-BROAD and the tree said so at once -
110 findings, the first ones read being CKAN package_search beside package_show?id={v}, a correct hop in a defect bucket. On a
query URL the last "/"-segment is `package_search?rows=100` and its `100` passed a "looks like an id" test. Narrowed: the
query strings must be identical, the difference must be in the last PATH segment, and the url's own segment must be
digit-dense. Ten fixtures run before the check on every lint run, and the over-broad version gets 3 of the 10 wrong, so the
set discriminates rather than merely passing. A row that means it says so with a `detail-self-hop-ok: <reason>` marker, as
page-offset-ok does.
verdict: SELF = every record's detail_key equals the id already in the url. NO-KEY = the key resolves on no record, so
hp_deepen() spends the budget and stamps _detail_error on every record - a disclosed failure to fetch a detail that does not
exist. WRONG-NS = the key resolves to an id from another namespace and the hop asks this endpoint for it (404s).
*** THE SECOND DEFECT IS NOW FIXED TOO (same day, the commit after the hop removals). ***
All 9 also carried ONE entity frozen into the url on a schedule, so each re-read one subject for ever and emitted that one
record's nested array. Each is now the entity pivot its own name claims - `{q}` in the path, interval 0, no page_walk, a
`.want` shape gate, and an array_path/id_keys/title_keys chosen from what the row's own DESCRIPTION says the record is. No
collector relabel was needed: registry_is_entity_pivot() reads interval 0, a non-`_` collector and a `{q`-token, and
`make registry-floor` reports 0 never-runs after the change.
The conversion needed a reading per host, not an inference from the others, and the pivot_reading column is that reading. Two
findings from it are worth more than the nine rows:
* DECLARING id_keys WAS NOT POLISH, IT WAS THE FIX. None of the nine declared one. Web NDL Authorities is JSON-LD, so an
authority record's only top-level scalars are @context, created, label, modified and uri - and with no id_keys the
fallback ends at the record's FIRST SCALAR, which is `@context`, identical on every record in the API. Every person the
pivot was ever asked about would have collapsed onto one uid, silently (rule 4b). A scheduled row reading ONE entity can
never show that; a pivot shows it on the second question.
* ONE OF THEM SETTLES RULE 4d FOR THE FAMILY, free. /reports/reportList/16928?baseReportTypeId=2 answers an EMPTY items
array where a server ignoring its path parameter would have handed back filer 15021's fifty reports. An honest empty for
an entity with no reports of that type is exactly what a pivot should do.
STILL UNMEASURED, and written down as such: br-ibge-municipio-detalhe's host timed out on both attempts from this container,
so its conversion rests on the row's own removed detail_url having templated that exact position (authored from a live probe)
rather than on a reading. Re-read it from somewhere with egress to servicodados.ibge.gov.br.

array of their one frozen record as the record set - historiskenavn (an establishment's former names), sideactivities and

should be AND whether a company register that answers for any CNPJ/organisasjonsnummer belongs on a 24 h schedule at all,
which is a question about the row's purpose rather than about its url. Three hosts, unmeasured from here so far.
